instruction:
Decoupling-Cap PDN Impedance

The board in /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb has a 3V3 power rail with a single 100 nF decoupling cap. The file /home/user/Desktop/target_z.csv defines the maximum allowed PDN impedance at 5 frequencies (10 kHz to 100 MHz). The file /home/user/Desktop/cap_models.csv lists available capacitor values with their ESR and ESL. The current single-cap PDN does not meet target impedance at all frequencies.

Add decoupling capacitors near the 3V3 rail to meet the target impedance at all 5 frequencies. Use the lumped PDN model: Z_total(f) = 1 / |Sigma_i( 1 / Z_cap_i(f) )| where Z_cap_i = ESR_i + j*(2*pi*f*ESL_i - 1/(2*pi*f*C_i)). Place caps within 5mm of the nearest 3V3 pad. Record the resulting impedance in a CSV.

Requirements:
1. /home/user/Desktop/pdn_analysis.csv has exactly 5 rows with columns freq_hz,z_ohm.
2. At every frequency, z_ohm <= target_ohm from /home/user/Desktop/target_z.csv.
3. All decoupling caps placed within 5mm of a 3V3 pad (center-to-center distance).
4. Cap count >= initial count (1 cap minimum).
5. Each added cap value matches an entry in /home/user/Desktop/cap_models.csv.
6. All caps placed within board outline (0,0)-(80,60).
7. No cap overlaps another footprint.

Write /home/user/Desktop/board.kicad_pcb and /home/user/Desktop/pdn_analysis.csv.
